title: Constant-source coherent transformation spaces as sections of a mapping family
statement:
Use the quasicategories, internal functor simplicial sets, coherent transformations and right-pinched mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the space-valued transport and coherent mapping bifunctor $H_{\mathcal E}$ of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification]. Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$. Let $J$ be a $\mathcal U$-small simplicial set, let $\mathcal E$ be a $\mathcal U'$-small quasicategory with $\mathcal U$-small mapping spaces, let $p:J\to\mathcal E$ be a coherent diagram, and let $x$ be an object of $\mathcal E$. Put $F_{x,p}=H_{\mathcal E}(x,p(-)):J\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ and write $\Delta_Jx$ and $\Delta_J*$ for the constant diagrams at $x$ and at the one-point space, respectively. Define $q_{x,p}:A_{x,p}\to J$ as the pullback along $p$ of the source-fixed arrow left fibration $\{x\}\times_{\mathcal E,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal E)\to\mathcal E$, where the last projection is $\operatorname{ev}_1$. Define $\Gamma_J(q_{x,p})$ to be the simplicial set whose $n$-simplices are maps $s:J\times\Delta^n\to A_{x,p}$ over the projection to $J$. There are equivalences of Kan complexes
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal E)}(\Delta_Jx,p)\simeq\Gamma_J(q_{x,p})\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})}(\Delta_J*,F_{x,p}).$$
These comparisons are coherent in $x$ contravariantly and in $p$ covariantly, and compatible with restriction along maps of small indexing simplicial sets. They identify a transformation $b:\Delta_Jx\to p$ with the section whose values are its arrows $b_j:x\to p(j)$, retaining every higher simplex. In particular, for a cone $\lambda:\Delta_Jl\to p$, postcomposition $f\mapsto\lambda\circ\Delta_Jf$ corresponds on the right to the coherent family $f\mapsto(\lambda_j\circ f)_{j\in J}$, on the entire space $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,l)$. The total space $A_{x,p}$ need only be $\mathcal U'$-small; its section space has a $\mathcal U$-small Kan model. Empty $J$ and empty mapping spaces are allowed.

source.place: Subsection 8.3.3, Hom-functors and their mapping-space interpretation, together with the section description in Subsection 7.4.1 (https://kerodon.net/tag/05QM). proof.text: Put $D=\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal E)$, $a=\Delta_Jx$, and $M_{x,p}=\operatorname{Map}_D(a,p)$. Since $J$ is small and $\mathcal E$ is a quasicategory, [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes $D$ a quasicategory and $M_{x,p}$ Kan. Initially work in a universe containing $\mathcal U'$ as an element: $D$ and its mapping spaces fit there, so subsequent applications of coherent Hom functoriality to $D$ are legitimate. No local $\mathcal U$-smallness of $D$ is assumed. Step 8 will descend the particular space $M_{x,p}$ to $\mathcal U$.

source.place: Hom-functors in a sufficiently large universe; setup for the explicit comparison

proof.text: Let $U_D(a,p)=\{a\}\times_{D,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,D)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,D}\{p\}$, as in [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]. Expanding the internal functor and pullback definitions in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], an $n$-simplex of this set is a map $h:J\times\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal E$ whose restriction at $0$ is constant at $x$ and whose restriction at $1$ is $p$ pulled back from $J$. An $n$-simplex of $\Gamma_J(q_{x,p})$ is exactly the same map: its $J$ coordinate is prescribed, and its arrow coordinate is $h$. Sending one description to the other and back changes no value. Operators restrict the $\Delta^n$ coordinate on both sides. Thus this is a simplicial isomorphism $c:U_D(a,p)\cong\Gamma_J(q_{x,p})$, not merely a bijection of vertices.

source.place: Agent argument: exponential law expanded degree by degree for the specified internal functor

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison] to the quasicategory $D$ from Step 1 and endpoints $a,p$. It gives a homotopy equivalence $j_D:M_{x,p}\to U_D(a,p)$ between Kan complexes. Compose with $c$ from Step 2 to obtain the first equivalence. Explicitly, an $n$-simplex $\sigma:J\times\Delta^{n+1}\to\mathcal E$ of $M_{x,p}$ goes to $h=\sigma\circ(\mathrm{id}_J\times\rho_n)$, where $\rho_n(t,0)=t$ and $\rho_n(t,1)=n+1$. At $n=0$ this sends the edge $b:\Delta_Jx\to p$ to precisely its arrow-valued section. The same formula retains the entire higher simplex. In particular $\Gamma_J(q_{x,p})$ is Kan.

source.place: Proposition 4.6.5.10, right-pinch inclusion, applied to the internal functor category

proof.text: By [lem-coef-space-transport-classification], $H_{\mathcal E}(x,-)$ classifies the source-fixed arrow left fibration. Its pullback along $p$ therefore represents $F_{x,p}$, with pullback compatibility giving exactly $q_{x,p}$. The constant functor $\Delta_J*$ is represented by $J\times*\to J$, canonically $J\to J$. Apply the mapping-space formula of that same node to these two representatives. Its right side is $\operatorname{Fun}_{/J}(J,A_{x,p})=\Gamma_J(q_{x,p})$ by its stated simplex formula. This gives the second displayed equivalence, read in the reverse direction. The node explicitly says that this mapping complex is Kan and that the equivalence preserves compositions, higher simplices and pullback of the base. Its hypotheses permit an arbitrary simplicial base $J$.

source.place: Section-space model for transformations from the constant point, using the full transport comparison stated in the cited node

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-relative-hom-evaluation] in the containing universe of Step 1 with $K=J$, $C=D$, $B=\mathcal E$, $i=\Delta_J$, $t=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal E}$, and $T:J\times D\to\mathcal E$ the internal evaluation map. The equality $T(j,\Delta_Jx)=x$ holds as a simplicial map on $J\times\mathcal E$, directly from the constant-diagram definition. The lemma therefore supplies a single coherent transformation $\varepsilon_{x,p}:\Delta_JH_D(\Delta_Jx,p)\to H_{\mathcal E}(x,p(-))$, natural on $\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}\times D$. Its explicit transport clause identifies the corresponding map over $J$ with $(j,\sigma)\mapsto\sigma(j,-)\circ\rho_n$ for $\sigma\in M_{x,p,n}$. This is exactly the adjoint of $c j_D$ in Steps 2–3, as an identification of full mapping spaces over $J$. Thus their comparison admits coherent dependence on $x,p$. This application uses the lemma's relative identification, including all $J$-simplices; it does not deduce coherence from separate vertex evaluations. Combined with the two-input coherent comparison in Step 4, it proves the required parameter naturality. The lemma's universe compatibility allows the arrow comparison to be used with the original locally $\mathcal U$-small Hom values. The actual arrow formula is unchanged by enlarging universes.

source.place: Agent application of the relative Hom evaluation lemma to internal evaluation; Definition 7.4.2.2 identifies the additional compatibility that was missing in the returned split.

proof.text: If $v:I\to J$ is any map of small simplicial sets, the pullback of $q_{x,p}$ is $q_{x,pv}$: both have the same prescribed arrow coordinate and base coordinate. Restricting the section represented by $h$ replaces $h$ by $h\circ(v\times\mathrm{id}_{\Delta^n}\times\mathrm{id}_{\Delta^1})$. This commutes strictly with $\mathrm{id}\times\rho_n$. Thus Step 3 is compatible with restriction, also by the functor-naturality clause of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison] for $D\to\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal E)$. Step 4 is compatible with restriction by the pullback clause of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification]. Both conclusions hold on every simplex.

source.place: Explicit naturality of the pinch map; transport base-change compatibility

proof.text: Fix $\lambda:\Delta_Jl\to p$ and put $N=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,l)$. The required map is $N\xrightarrow{(\Delta_J)_*}M_{x,\Delta_Jl}\xrightarrow{\lambda\circ-}M_{x,p}$. Applying the constant-diagram functor to right-pinched simplices gives the first arrow, with canonical composition as in [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality] and [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. Apply the postcomposition naturality square of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-hom-evaluation] with $c=\Delta_Jl$, $c'=p$, $u=\lambda$, and the evaluation data of Step 5. After precomposing its upper-left corner by $\Delta_JN$, it identifies the composite with $H_{\mathcal E}(x,\lambda)\circ\varepsilon_{x,\Delta_Jl}\circ\Delta_J(\Delta_J)_*$. The last two factors are the constant family at the identity map of $N$: their transport formula evaluates the constant arrow family $f$ at $j$, giving the same $f$ on every simplex of $J$. The lower map is the single coherent family of postcompositions along $\lambda:J\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal E$. Hence the composite is $f\mapsto(\lambda_j\circ f)_{j\in J}$. The new lemma identifies this naturality square with its map of total spaces over $J$, including the $J\times\Delta^1$ data and arbitrary parameter simplices in $N$. It therefore gives the claimed map on the entire space, rather than only the vertex-fiber formula. Step 4 carries the same coherent square to the right-hand transformation space.

source.place: Agent application of the relative Hom evaluation postcomposition square; the new lemma isolates the transport compatibility over the entire indexing shape.

proof.text: The fibers of $q_{x,p}$ are essentially $\mathcal U$-small since they represent $H_{\mathcal E}(x,p(j))$. As $J$ is $\mathcal U$-small, [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] permits a $\mathcal U$-small representative $q':A'\to J$ of $F_{x,p}$. The full mapping comparison in that node identifies $\Gamma_J(q')$ and $\Gamma_J(q_{x,p})$ with the same mapping space from $\Delta_J*$ to $F_{x,p}$; equivalently an equivalence between the representatives induces an equivalence on these section spaces. The simplices of $\Gamma_J(q')$ form subsets of the sets of maps $J\times\Delta^n\to A'$, so form a $\mathcal U$-small simplicial set. It is Kan by the same node. This is the required small Kan model, without asserting that $A_{x,p}$ itself is small. If $J$ is empty, Step 2 has a unique map in each degree and the section space is a point; Steps 3 and 4 give the same answer for the other two spaces. For $J=\Delta^0$ they reduce to the usual mapping space, which can be empty. More generally an empty fiber at a vertex prevents a section, and all the comparisons still apply: no cited statement requires nonempty fibers.
